### Basic FastAPI App with SlowAPI

Source: https://github.com/laurents/slowapi/blob/master/_autodocs/README.md

A minimal FastAPI application demonstrating SlowAPI integration for rate limiting. Ensure to add the middleware and exception handler, and initialize the limiter.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded
from slowapi.middleware import SlowAPIASGIMiddleware
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

app = FastAPI()
limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)

app.add_middleware(SlowAPIASGIMiddleware)
app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)
app.state.limiter = limiter

@app.get("/api/data")
@limiter.limit("100/minute")
async def get_data(request: Request):
    return {"data": []}
```

--------------------------------

### Cost-Based Limiting in FastAPI

Source: https://github.com/laurents/slowapi/blob/master/_autodocs/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md

Implement cost-based rate limiting by defining custom cost functions for different endpoints. This example shows charging based on upload size and request complexity.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, UploadFile, File
from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded
from slowapi.middleware import SlowAPIASGIMiddleware
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

app = FastAPI()

# Calculate cost based on request characteristics
async def get_upload_cost(request: Request) -> int:
    # Get body size as cost
    try:
        body = await request.body()
        # 1 point per 1MB
        return max(1, len(body) // (1024 * 1024))
    except:
        return 1

def get_compute_cost(request: Request) -> int:
    # Charge more for complex requests
    complexity = request.headers.get("X-Complexity", "low")
    costs = {"low": 1, "medium": 5, "high": 10}
    return costs.get(complexity, 1)

limiter = Limiter(
    key_func=get_remote_address,
    default_limits=["1000/hour"]  # Cost units per hour
)

app.add_middleware(SlowAPIASGIMiddleware)
app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)
app.state.limiter = limiter

@app.post("/api/upload")
@limiter.limit("100/hour", cost=get_upload_cost)
async def upload(request: Request, file: UploadFile):
    return {"uploaded": file.filename}

@app.post("/api/compute")
@limiter.limit("1000/hour", cost=get_compute_cost)
async def compute(request: Request, data: dict):
    return {"computed": data}
```

--------------------------------

### Valid Rate Limit Configuration

Source: https://github.com/laurents/slowapi/blob/master/_autodocs/api-reference/errors.md

Use this format to apply a valid rate limit to an endpoint. The limit is applied during decorator initialization.

```python
from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.middleware import SlowAPIMiddleware
from starlette.requests import Request

limiter = Limiter()

@limiter.limit("10/minute")  # Valid
async def endpoint1(request: Request):
    pass
```

--------------------------------

### Multiple Rate Limits

Source: https://github.com/laurents/slowapi/blob/master/_autodocs/RATE_LIMIT_STRINGS.md

Apply multiple rate limits (per second, minute, and hour) to an endpoint. The request must satisfy all limits.

```python
import asyncio
from starlette.requests import Request

from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)


# Request must satisfy all limits to proceed
@limiter.limit("10/second;100/minute;1000/hour")
async def comprehensive_limit(request: Request):
    pass
```

--------------------------------

### Stacked Rate Limit Decorators

Source: https://github.com/laurents/slowapi/blob/master/_autodocs/RATE_LIMIT_STRINGS.md

Multiple '@limiter.limit()' decorators can be stacked on a single endpoint. This combines the limits, effectively acting as if they were specified in a single decorator with semicolon-separated values.

```python
@limiter.limit("100/minute")
@limiter.limit("1000/hour")
async def endpoint(request: Request):
    pass

# Equivalent to: @limiter.limit("100/minute;1000/hour")
```

```python
import re
from email.utils import parseaddr


def is_valid_email(address: str) -> bool:
    _, addr = parseaddr(address)
    if not addr:
        return False
    if '@' not in addr:
        return False
    local, domain = addr.rsplit('@', 1)
    if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+$', local):
        return False
    if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$', domain):
        return False
    return True
```

Uses `email.utils.parseaddr` (stdlib) instead of raw regex on the input string, so quoted local parts and whitespace stripping are handled correctly. Only stdlib – no dependency. Validates structural shape after parsing, which covers the vast majority of real-world addresses without over-engineering into RFC 5322 full compliance.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded

async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):

    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)


@app.get("/your-endpoint")
@limiter.limit("5/minute")
```
